_strings.@@ce1671ffe97d: Treaty conformity — AL does NOT conform to federal tax treaties: income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is STILL taxable by AL. Do not carry a federal treaty exclusion onto the state return. (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state's Internal Revenue Code conformity date and its deduction/credit conformity are separate questions; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Alabama does NOT start the return from federal adjusted gross income. Both the resident Form 40 and the nonresident Form 40NR build Alabama income from their own line items computed under Alabama law (Form 40NR Line 5 'Wages, Salaries, Tips, Etc.' from Schedule W-2; Line 6/8 'Other Income'; separate interest/dividend lines), not by importing a federal AGI figure. Because the federal-AGI-conformity flow-through does not exist here, a treaty exclusion that is already netted out of federal AGI does NOT automatically carry to the Alabama return. The 23f40nrbk.pdf booklet (page 12, Line 8) is explicit on the only foreign-income mechanism it recognizes: 'All foreign income must be reported on your return, in order to receive any foreign income exclusion,' and that exclusion is the IRC sec. 911 foreign EARNED income exclusion, claimed as a separate negative-line credit with federal Form 2555 attached. There is NO Alabama line, schedule, or instruction that recognizes or excludes income exempt under a U.S. income-TAX TREATY. Given (a) the separate Alabama income build-up rather than a federal-AGI start, and (b) the affirmative 'report all foreign income' rule with only a sec. 911-style exclusion path, conformity to federal treaty exemptions is NOT established on any .gov page. Per conservative handling this is set false and flagged. See unverified/notes.

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: Form 40, line 17: 'Income Tax due. Enter amount from tax table or check if from Form NOL-85A' (line 16: 'Taxable income. Subtract line 15 from line 10.'); booklet Line 17 instructions: 'You must figure your tax from the Tax Tables unless you are claiming a carryover or carryback Net Operating Loss from another year.' This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Base guidance: Supply 2023 Alabama Form 40, page 1, line 16 'Taxable income. Subtract line 15 from line 10.' Alabama does NOT start from federal AGI: line 10 Alabama adjusted gross income is built from Alabama line items (line 8 total income minus line 9 adjustments), and line 15 total deductions = line 11 (itemized OR sliding standard deduction) + line 12 (FEDERAL income tax deduction, from the Federal Income Tax Deduction Worksheet) + line 13 (personal exemption $1,500/$3,000) + line 14 (income-dependent dependent exemption). All of those subtractions must already be taken on the form before line 16 — this op subtracts nothing further. Tax-table mandate: the 2023 Form 40 booklet (Line 17 instructions) states 'You must figure your tax from the Tax Tables unless you are claiming a carryover or carryback Net Operating Loss from another year.' The Tax Table (booklet pp. 25-30) covers taxable income under $100,000 in bands (mostly $100 wide) priced at the band midpoint, so bracket math may differ by a few dollars within table bands; the filed form must use the table. Over $100,000: the booklet's worksheet (p. 30) computes tax as $4,958.00 (Single/MFS/Head of Family) or $4,918.00 (MFJ) plus 5% of taxable income over $100,000. Those printed constants are each $2 LESS than the exact cumulative bracket sums ($4,960 / $4,920) because they carry forward the last tax-table row's midpoint value; above $100,000 the tax the form produces is therefore $2 lower than pure bracket math. Alabama does not start from federal AGI: Form 40 income is built from Alabama line items (line 8 total income, line 9 adjustments, line 10 Alabama AGI). Supply line 16 exactly as computed on the form. FEDERAL income tax deduction quirk: Alabama allows a base deduction for federal income tax liability (Form 40 line 12; Federal Income Tax Deduction Worksheet, booklet p. 31: 2023 Form 1040/1040-SR/1040-NR line 22 plus Form 8960 line 17 net investment income tax, minus refundable EIC, Additional Child Tax Credit, American Opportunity Credit, and Form 2439 credits). It is already inside the line 16 base this op consumes — do not re-subtract it. standard_deduction is NOT shipped because Alabama's standard deduction slides with Alabama AGI (booklet p. 9 chart, per Act 2022-292 amounts): MFJ $8,500 (AL AGI $0-$25,999) phasing down to $5,000 at $35,500 and above; MFS $4,250 ($0-$12,999) down to $2,500 at $17,750 and above; Head of Family $5,200 ($0-$25,999) down to $2,500 at $35,500 and above; Single $3,000 ($0-$25,999) down to $2,500 at $35,500 and above. Take it from the chart on Form 40 line 11; it is already inside line 16. Personal exemption (Form 40 line 13) is $1,500 (Single or Married Filing Separately) / $3,000 (Married Filing Jointly or Head of Family), printed on the Form 40 filing-status boxes 1-4. It is a base reduction, but it is already inside the line 16 base this op consumes, so it is NOT shipped as an engine exemption. Dependent exemption (Form 40 line 14) is income-dependent and NOT shipped: $1,000 per dependent when Alabama AGI (line 10) is $0-$50,000; $500 when $50,001-$100,000; $300 when over $100,000 (booklet p. 8 chart). It is already inside line 16 — claim it on the form, not through this op. One rate schedule covers Single, Married Filing Separately, and Head of Family (2% on the first $500, 4% on the next $2,500, 5% over $3,000); Married Filing Jointly has its own schedule (2% on the first $1,000, 4% on the next $5,000, 5% over $6,000). Alabama has no qualifying-surviving-spouse filing status (Form 40 boxes are Single / Married filing joint / Married filing separate / Head of Family, and the booklet's Head-of-Family definition requires the individual 'is not a surviving spouse'). The engine's QSS-to-MFJ mapping does not correspond to an Alabama status — a filer widowed before 2023 files Single or Head of Family in Alabama, so do not rely on the MFJ schedule for a federal QSS filer. The 2%/4%/5% schedule text is printed on the ADOR FAQ 'What is Alabama's Individual Income Tax Rate?' (https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/faqs/what-is-alabamas-individual-income-tax-rate/) and was verified numerically against the 2023 booklet's Tax Table rows and over-$100,000 worksheet. Retirement exclusion (NEW for 2023, Act 2022-294): 2023 Schedule RS (Form 40 or Form 40NR), Part II line 10 (primary) and Part III line 10 (spouse) — 'If "Yes", each taxpayer is eligible up to $6,000 not to exceed the Retirement Income Taxable to Alabama on line 9' — excludes up to $6,000 of taxable retirement income per taxpayer who is 65 or older (2023 Schedule RS Instructions, Line 10: 'eligible for an exclusion of retirement income up to $6,000, not to exceed the amount taxable to Alabama on Line 9'); the 2023 Form 40 and Form 40NR booklets' What's New (p.2): 'exempts the first $6,000 of taxable retirement income for those 65 years of age or older.' The net figure (Schedule RS Part IV line 3) lands on Form 40 page 2 Part I line 4 / Form 40NR page 2 Part I line 3 column B, so it is already inside the line 16 base this op consumes and is NOT shipped as an engine exemption. Alabama Accountability Tax Credit – School Transfer Credit (Schedule AATC, Schedule OC Part K): per the 2023 Schedule OC Instructions (p.3) the credit is 'the lesser of 80 percent of the average annual state cost attendance for a public K-12 student during the applicable tax year or the actual cost of attending a nonfailing public school or nonpublic school'; the 2023 Schedule AATC face pre-prints that 80% figure as $4,795.00 on lines 7, 16, 25 and 34 (one block per student, up to four; line 9 'Enter the lesser of line 7 or line 8'), with line 37 carried to Schedule OC Section B Part K line K1 and the refundable amount through Schedule OC Section F line F1 (summed on line F4) to page 1 line 25 of Form 40 or Form 40NR. The booklets and the Schedule OC Instructions do not state the dollar figure; only the Schedule AATC face prints it. calc.state_tax applies no Alabama credits; the constant is recorded here for the Schedule AATC port.
